newsitem.title: USA: Foiled defection leads Chinese reporter to suicide - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Foiled defection leads Chinese reporter to suicide - NYT.

text.p: Just days after being recalled from his post in Washington, Chinese journalist Wei Guoqiang committed suicide in Beijing last weekend after a colleague said he had been discovered preparing to defect, The New York Times reported on Wednesday.
It said Wei, 47, was the Washington bureau chief of the New China News Agency Xinhua and a well-known figure among foreign journalists in the U.S. capital.

The Times quoted one of Wei's colleagues as saying he was recalled to Beijing in late March after a Washington co-worker discovered him preparing documents to support a political asylum application in the United States for himself, his wife and his 17-year-old daughter.
Wei was a specialist on American affairs and served a first tour in Washington from the late 1980s to 1993. He was appointed Xinhua's Washington bureau chief in early 1996.

The New York Times in its report from Beijing said Chinese news organisations, including Wei's own agency, have made no public mention of his death, but it was confirmed by several of his colleagues. They said a memorial service was planned for Thursday.
